entities.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the God whom the man and his wife hear walking in the garden, the same Yahweh who brought the woman to the man in Genesis 2:22.
The repeated name יַהְוֶה identifies the one from whom the couple hides as the same Yahweh they have just heard.

review.translation: [Then they heard|0] [the sound of|2,1] [Yahweh|3] [God|4] [walking about|5] [in the garden|6] [in the breeze of|7] [the day|8], [but|9] [the man|10] [and his wife|11] [hid|9] [from the presence of|12] [Yahweh|13] [God|14] [among|15] [the tree|16]{s} [of|16] [the garden|17].

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks קוֹל יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים as the direct object. The man and his wife heard the sound of Yahweh God walking in the garden and then hid.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces קוֹל יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, “the sound of Yahweh God,” as the definite direct object of וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ, “they heard.”
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in the short form אֶת, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶת־קוֹל יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים means “they heard the sound of Yahweh God.” The participle מִתְהַלֵּךְ describes him walking in the garden and identifies his movement as the source of the sound.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In קוֹל יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, “the sound of Yahweh God,” יַהְוֶה names the one whom the man and his wife hear walking in the garden.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun with no prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In קוֹל יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, “the sound of Yahweh God,” אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to the name יַהְוֶה and designates the same individual.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: They hear the sound of יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים walking about. The participle presents the walking as ongoing when they hear it, and בַּגָּן locates it in the garden.
analysis.morphology: Hitpael active participle, masculine singular absolute

analysis.evidence: בַּגָּן gives the location of מִתְהַלֵּךְ, “walking about.” The garden is mentioned again in עֵץ הַגָּן, “the trees of the garden.”
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article הַ, followed by a common noun, singular absolute, of common gender.

analysis.evidence: רוּחַ is in construct with הַיּוֹם, giving “the breeze of the day.” With לְ, the phrase describes the setting of the walk in the garden.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition לְ plus a common-gender noun in the singular construct state.

analysis.evidence: In לְרוּחַ הַיּוֹם, “at the breeze of the day,” הַיּוֹם completes the construct phrase and identifies the breeze with the daylight period. The phrase gives the time of the walk in the garden.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הַ־.
analysis.sense: daylight, the day as against night

draft.change: Add the root חבא with the Hithpael sense “hide oneself.”
draft.definition: In the Hithpael, to hide oneself from sight.
draft.evidence: In Gen.3.8 the man and his wife take cover among the garden trees when they hear Yahweh God.

analysis.evidence: After hearing Yahweh God, the man and his wife hide themselves. מִפְּנֵי יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים identifies whom they hide from, and בְּתוֹךְ עֵץ הַגָּן places them among the trees of the garden.
analysis.morphology: Hithpael wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed narrative וַ. The singular verb precedes the compound subject הָאָדָם וְאִשְׁתּוֹ and agrees with its first member.

analysis.evidence: In הָאָדָם וְאִשְׁתּוֹ (“the man and his wife”), the definite article identifies the particular man in the garden narrative. The suffix on וְאִשְׁתּוֹ refers back to him. Together they form the subject of וַיִּתְחַבֵּא (“hid”).
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state with the prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: In הָאָדָם וְאִשְׁתּוֹ, the suffix refers to הָאָדָם, identifying the woman who hides with the man as his wife.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus a feminine singular construct noun with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ.

analysis.evidence: The man and his wife hide among the trees. After וַיִּתְחַבֵּא ‘hid,’ מִפְּנֵי introduces יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים as the one from whose presence they hide.
analysis.morphology: Compound preposition formed from מִן and פְּנֵי, the plural construct of פָּנִים. The nun of מִן assimilates to the following pe.

analysis.evidence: In מִפְּנֵי יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, “from the presence of Yahweh God,” יַהְוֶה names the one from whom the man and his wife hide.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In מִפְּנֵי יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה and identifies the one from whose presence the man and his wife hide.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute in form, with singular reference.

draft.change: Assign the occurrence to the existing tavek-among sense of תָּוֶךְ and clarify the collective complement in its Genesis 3:8 evidence.
draft.definition: With בְּ and a collective complement, תָּוֶךְ locates someone among the members of the group.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 3:8, בְּתוֹךְ specifies the hiding place, and עֵץ הַגָּן identifies the trees that surround the man and his wife.

analysis.evidence: בְּתוֹךְ עֵץ הַגָּן answers where the man and his wife hid. עֵץ הַגָּן denotes the trees of the garden collectively, so בְּתוֹךְ places them among those trees.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בְּ “in” + תוֹךְ, masculine singular construct of תָּוֶךְ, governing עֵץ הַגָּן.
analysis.sense: among, in the midst of (a company)

analysis.evidence: In בְּתוֹךְ עֵץ הַגָּן, “among the trees of the garden,” עֵץ is in construct with הַגָּן. The singular refers collectively to the trees among which the man and his wife hide.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In עֵץ הַגָּן, “the trees of the garden,” הַגָּן identifies the garden whose trees provide cover for the man and his wife. The same garden appears earlier in בַּגָּן, “in the garden.”
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a common noun, singular absolute.
